biography.plain_text: Robert Cohen-Skalli, known as Robert Skalli, is a French wine entrepreneur. He expanded his family’s wine business in Sète, developing Fortant de France into an international brand. The grandson of a vineyard owner in Algeria, he sold the group’s wineries and brands in the Languedoc and Rhône Valley to Boisset in 2011.

long_biography.plain_text:
A visit to California convinced French wine entrepreneur Robert Cohen-Skalli, known as Robert Skalli, that grape-variety labels could open new markets for Languedoc wines. Working with three growers and a cooperative, he encouraged new plantings of Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Cabernet Sauvignon. Technical advice and commercial partnerships connected changes in the vineyards to demand overseas.

In Napa Valley, he bought land and designed and built the St. Supéry estate winery. When its first chief executive, Michaela Rodeno, arrived, she challenged the proposed branding, low-price strategy and release schedule. Skalli had already committed substantial resources to the vineyards and winery, but accepted her argument for a different approach. He gave her a year to rework the launch.
